claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with a few basics:

1. **How many children do you have or are responsible for?** And what are their names (or you can use initials if you prefer)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and want to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child I'm asking about - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you some questions about Alex:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, but Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep - such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or other expenses?** If yes, approximately how much do you contribute per month?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with things like clothes and other expenses. I give about £26 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Now I need to ask:

**Who does Alex currently live with?** (For example, does he live with your ex-partner, another family member, or someone else?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. This is an important question:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she isn't claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**For Alex:**
- Alex is 11 years old, which is under the age limit of 16 (or under 20 if in approved education or training)
- Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing £26 per week towards his upkeep for things like clothes and other expenses
- According to the Child Benefit rules, you can still be considered responsible for a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them
- Since you're contributing £26 per week, which meets or exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount, you qualify as being responsible for Alex
- Importantly, Alex's mother is not currently claiming Child Benefit for him, and only one person can claim for each child

**What to do next:**
You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Important note:** Please be aware that if either you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. This doesn't affect your eligibility to claim, but it may mean you need to pay back some or all of the benefit through your tax return.

Do you have any questions about claiming?
